payload.note: Conformal-curvature bubble checkpoint: in four dimensions A is one seventy-second of the scalar-curvature-squared functional for g=Omega squared delta. The stereographic round four-sphere gives an exact noncompact critical bubble with A=16 pi squared over 3. A positive-floor family has residual and Euler gradient in closed form and quotient asymptotic (864/5)(a/rho)^2. Matching its transition radius to torus size L leaves a nonzero formal normalized coefficient 54/(5 pi^4), while periodic gluing contributes at the same L^-4 order. Thus finite-volume uniqueness does not supply compactness, but no periodic counterexample is proved. The next gate is the complete smooth periodic Green-function bubble coefficient or a quantitative compactness theorem; Witten, Gibbs H^-1, continuum, Born, Krein, and Lorentzian claims remain open.
